ledger.claim: The trip record's own distances establish the deviation, so no 'within tolerance' answer is open to the driver: the actual route was 16.8 km against a recommended 15.3 km, a deviation of 1.50 km, and the record's own tolerance check reads within_tolerance false against a 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace confirms which route was taken — the vehicle left the recommended route at the ECP / Fort Road exit at 17:58:49 and rejoined it at Bedok South Road at 18:12:42 — and the trip record carries the matching route_deviation_detected and route_rejoined events. The rider paid distance the recommended route did not require.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record, and the refund matrix therefore puts it in row (d). POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory here overlaps the window, but its own derived facts record intersects_route as null and justifies_reroute as null, with the stated reason that the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route — the element the clause turns on is left unresolved. Its text directs drivers only to 'Avoid lanes 2 and 3', which leaves the ECP open, and it carries no severity; an advisory of that kind does not show that the recommended route could not be taken. With the traffic element unproven, the case is one of not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km: refund of the excess distance fare in full under POL-RD-24(d).

The amount the rider is owed on row (d) is the excess distance fare, computed as the policy prescribes: deviation 1.50 km times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, without surge, which the fare record's own derived money block puts at 1.08 SGD. The rider seeks that amount in full as a PARTIAL_REFUND, and the fare record shows refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, so nothing has been returned to the rider to date. The rider's claim asked for 5.00 SGD; the policy's measure of the overcharge is the excess distance fare, and the rider asks for that measure in full rather than the larger figure claimed.

The chat log does not move this case out of row (d). It shows only that the driver messaged the rider at 17:55:39 stating the plan and that the rider replied 'Sure no problem' at 17:56:14, before the vehicle left the route at 17:58:49. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires traffic justification as a separate and cumulative element alongside informing and agreement, and row (d) turns only on the absence of justification with a deviation over 1 km — it says nothing about informing or agreement. A rider's acknowledgment of a plan the driver had already formed cannot supply a missing traffic justification or convert an unjustified reroute into a row (a) case; under POL-RD-21 what the acknowledgment establishes is that this deviation was agreed, not that it was justified.

If the judge finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be established on this record, then a fact the refund matrix needs — the traffic element of POL-RD-23 — is unestablished, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated with the open question stated rather than an outcome inferred from the gap. On that alternative the ruling cannot stand as NO_ACTION either: with the justification element unresolved, a ruling upholding the charge cannot reach the 0.80 confidence POL-RD-25 requires for an AI route-deviation ruling, and escalation follows there too. ESCALATE under POL-GEN-03 holds the amount rather than collecting it, so on this alternative as well the rider does not carry the disputed charge while the intersection question is resolved by a human reviewer.

The deviation is established on the platform's recorded distances, not on the trace: actual 16.80 km less optimal 15.30 km is 1.50 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 uses the trip record's distances precisely because a sparse trace understates a route's length, and this 59-fix trace measures only 14.177 km — below the recommended route length — so it cannot be used to re-measure.

The driver gave notice before the point of deviation. His in-app message MSG-06003-003 was sent at 17:55:39 and read at 17:55:48: 'Hi, accident on ECP after Marine Parade, I exit Fort Road and go Marine Parade Road instead ok?' The route_deviation_detected event is timestamped 17:58:49, over three minutes later, so the POL-RD-21 obligation to inform the rider 'before or at the point of deviation' is met, and no verbal notice or call recording is needed because the chat log carries the notice.

The rider acknowledged the deviation before it happened: her reply MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', was sent at 17:56:14, again before the 17:58:49 deviation point. Under POL-RD-21, where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and this chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and reconciles to trip_record.chat_message_count of 4.

The reroute was traffic-justified. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, issued 17:34:22 and valid to 18:49:22 — overlapping the trip window of 17:49:22 to 18:18:22. ACCIDENT is within POL-RD-23's admissible 'incident' vocabulary, and the artifact is a third-party traffic record, not the driver's assertion.

The advisory sits on the recommended route. Its own fields give road 'East Coast Parkway (ECP)', direction 'towards Changi' and location 'after Marine Parade exit' — the same road and the same direction of travel that the recommended route lists ('North Bridge Road, Raffles Avenue, East Coast Parkway (ECP), Bedok South Road, Simei Street 3'). The driver's contemporaneous message independently names the same incident, 'accident on ECP after Marine Parade'. The artifact flags route intersection as 'undetermined' and leaves it to the Judge; nothing in the record places the advisory anywhere other than the ECP carriageway the recommended route uses towards this dropoff.

On POL-RD-24's matrix this case falls in row (a): the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed and agreed, and the deviation was over 1 km. Row (a) pays no refund, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. Rows (b) and (d) are the refund rows, and neither applies once justification and the rider's agreement are established.

The rider's figure of 5.00 SGD is unsupported on the policy's own arithmetic even on the reading most favourable to her. The only refund available on this matrix is the excess distance fare: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge applied. Row (b) or (d) would therefore move 1.08 SGD, not 5.00 SGD, and the rider's claim for the balance fails in any event.

NO_ACTION is the driver's outcome here. The rider filed this dispute, the fare stands charged at 26.04 SGD and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and it preserves the present state, leaving the metered fare the driver earned intact rather than restoring anything.

There is no open question requiring escalation under POL-GEN-26. Each fact POL-RD-24 needs — the deviation distance, the notice to the rider, the rider's agreement and the traffic justification — is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 caps nothing and the record is sufficient for a ruling.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is decided on the platform's own records, and the rider's claim is not supported. The present state stands.

The deviation is real, and I accept it. POL-RD-22 measures it from the trip record's recorded distances, not from the trace: 16.80 km actual less 15.30 km recommended is 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Both sides agree on this, and the GPS trace (which measures only 14.177 km) is not used to re-measure, exactly as POL-RD-22 provides.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260923-1113 records an ACCIDENT on the East Coast Parkway (towards Changi) after the Marine Parade exit, valid 17:34:22 to 18:49:22, and so overlapping the trip window (17:49:22 to 18:18:22). ACCIDENT is an admissible 'incident' type. The advisory's road (ECP), direction (towards Changi) and location (after Marine Parade exit) place it on the recommended route's ECP segment, which the recommended route uses from Raffles Avenue through to Bedok South Road; the recommended route does not leave the ECP until Bedok South Road, so an incident after the Marine Parade exit lies on it. The artifact leaves intersection 'undetermined' for the Judge, and on these fields I decide it intersects. The rider's point that the message says 'avoid lanes 2 and 3' does not change this: POL-RD-23 asks whether the advisory intersects the route and shows an incident, not whether the road was impassable.

The driver informed the rider before the deviation, and the rider agreed. MSG-06003-003 was sent at 17:55:39 and read at 17:55:48; MSG-06003-004, 'Sure no problem', was sent at 17:56:14; the route_deviation_detected event is at 17:58:49. POL-RD-21's notice was therefore given before the point of deviation, and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, so the deviation is agreed.

On POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and it is row (a): traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — no refund. Rows (b) and (d) are the refund rows and neither applies. The rider's stated figure of 5.00 SGD is unsupported in any event: the only refund the matrix ever yields is the excess distance fare, which on these figures would be 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, with no surge. The rider filed this dispute, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is read against her claim and leaves the metered fare of 26.04 SGD charged and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 undisturbed; it restores nothing to the driver.

The rider's alternative — that the traffic element is unestablished and the case must be escalated under POL-GEN-26 — fails. The fact POL-RD-23 needs is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-ADVIS-06003-01), and it is established from that artifact's own fields; there is no missing or impaired evidence and so no open question. POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence requirement is met at 0.85, and POL-GEN-22 (5.00 SGD contested, below the 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flags) permits the AI ruling to stand.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
